name: Amazon API Gateway
summary: AWS’s managed API front door: REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs that authenticate, throttle and route calls to Lambda and other backends.
intro: API Gateway gives you an HTTPS endpoint, maps each route (a method plus a path, like `POST /orders`) to an integration, and handles auth and throttling on the way. Integrations can be a Lambda function, any HTTP URL, a private service behind a VPC link, or an AWS API called directly, such as putting a message on SQS. It comes in three products. REST APIs have the most features: API keys and usage plans, per-client throttling, request validation, caching, AWS WAF and private endpoints. HTTP APIs are leaner and cheaper ($1.00 instead of $3.50 per million requests in US East) and add built-in JWT authorisers. WebSocket APIs keep connections open for up to 2 hours and route each message by a field in its body.

Every request is metered against an account-wide throttle, 10,000 requests per second by default in most regions, using a token bucket with a burst of 5,000. The best-known limit is the integration timeout: 29 seconds for REST and WebSocket APIs and 30 seconds for HTTP APIs. Since June 2024 you can ask AWS to raise it for Regional and private REST APIs, possibly in exchange for a lower throttle quota. Since November 2025 REST APIs of every endpoint type can also stream responses for up to 15 minutes and past the 10 MB payload cap, as long as the stream doesn’t sit idle (5 minutes on Regional and private endpoints, 30 seconds on edge-optimised ones). HTTP and WebSocket APIs stay capped.
strengths: No servers: you pay only for the calls you receive and the data sent out
Auth, throttling and usage plans in front of Lambda without writing that code yourself
Direct AWS service integrations can write to SQS, Step Functions or DynamoDB with no function in between
WebSocket APIs manage the open connections, so your backend only handles messages
limits: The 29- or 30-second integration timeout rules out long synchronous calls unless you raise it or stream the response on a REST API
Request and response payloads are capped at 10 MB (streamed REST responses excepted), and WebSocket messages at 128 KB
REST vs HTTP is a real fork: caching, WAF, API keys and request validation exist only on REST APIs
Per-request pricing gets expensive at sustained high volume, where an ALB is often cheaper

snippet.title: Quick-create an HTTP API in front of a Lambda function

story: Before 2015, putting an API on the internet meant building far more than the API. Each team wrote its own authorization, access control, traffic limits, monitoring and versioning, and often maintained client SDKs for several languages too. As Jeff Barr put it, the code devoted to that infrastructure “can dwarf the actual implementation of the service”.

AWS launched Amazon API Gateway on 9 July 2015 to take that layer off developers’ hands. You described routes, imported existing Swagger definitions if you had them, and pointed each one at a backend. Paired with Lambda, it let teams build APIs that were “totally server-less”: no machines to run even for the front door. Custom domains were served through CloudFront, and the console could generate JavaScript, iOS and Android SDKs.

The service then split into products for different needs. WebSocket APIs arrived in December 2018 for chat and games. In December 2019 AWS previewed HTTP APIs, a slimmer version for the common case of proxying to Lambda or an HTTP backend, at up to 71% less than REST APIs. More recently, longer timeouts and response streaming were added for generative AI workloads that take more than 29 seconds to answer.

choices.choice: Serve APIs through CloudFront’s edge by default
choices.why: The original API endpoints ran behind CloudFront, so callers anywhere connected to a nearby edge. In 2017 Regional endpoints were added because callers in the same Region didn’t need the extra hop.
Each route maps straight to a Lambda function, an HTTP URL or an AWS API call, so a whole backend can exist without any instance to patch or scale.

choices.choice: Import Swagger and generate client SDKs
choices.why: Mobile and web teams were spending time hand-writing SDKs for every platform. Driving the API from a machine-readable definition let the gateway produce them.

choices.choice: A cheaper, leaner HTTP API alongside REST
choices.why: Many serverless APIs just proxy to Lambda or an HTTP backend. HTTP APIs leave out API keys, caching and request validation so that common case can be offered for less.

timeline.text: Amazon API Gateway launches on 9 July for REST APIs
Regional endpoints, and VPC Link to reach private backends via an NLB
Private APIs inside VPCs; WebSocket APIs arrive in December
HTTP APIs, previewed in December 2019, become generally available in March
Regional and private REST APIs can raise the 29-second integration timeout
REST APIs gain response streaming, with streams up to 15 minutes long
